name: lagoon_keyframe
intent: The approved key frame (15 Nov, Blender) as a place in the open-world lagoon: a weathered head with a gate (focal point, upper left third), warm coral heads leading in from the near sand (table coral as the colour accent), the grown meadow framing the right edge, open sand and a clear blue lane for the fish school. Restrained, Japanese garden: three rock masses (focal arch, one behind, one far), five coral heads, one meadow bed, the rest is sand and water.
frame: key frame layout metres (Blender: x right, y forward, z up). godot = anchor_yaw * (x, z, -y) + anchor
source: papers/process/art_bible/style_level/keyframe/src/layout.json (scene.py cam slice) ported 1:1; upgrades are listed per item in 'why'; rocks from layout_arch_g.json (the arch as focal point, coordinator 21 Nov 05:16Z)
seat: every item is dropped onto the drawn ground under its own footprint (ray to the floor collision), as habitat.seat_blades did

items.role: focal head: Rock's heads_v18c (Gary's pick 21 Nov), gate turned to face the key camera
items.why: upgrade: v18c replaces kit v18 b0 (layout_arch_g.json, Style 21 Nov); set back along the key camera's ray from 10.6 to 13.0 m (Fable r2 + measured r3: 10.6 m cut the top, 16.5 m lost it in the haze); r6 (Fable r5 "hard base line"): its foot, the gate fall Terrain grows from this head's own fall record (14 blocks at both mouths, roof and wear chips, seabed/tools/gate_fall.py v3) plus the rubble_rule v11 apron round its real outline; r7: its sand skirt from the key frame rig's habitat.bank (0.12 m bank against the foot, arch_set.sh), since v18c has no kit skirt; r7 SILHOUETTE (Gary 27 Nov 18:42Z silhouette before detail): the key frame's massif spans 5-63 % of the frame width with its top 13 % down; r6 ran 18-93 % with the top cut off. So the head turned 13 deg left about the camera and set back to 16 m (r7b at 17 deg / 17.5 m measured 1-50 %, r7c tuned to the key frame's 5-63 %), its yaw turned with it so the gate still faces the camera

items.role: mid-ground head in front of the arch's left foot (the key frame's own near head, kit b0)
items.why: r9 SILHOUETTE (Gary kept the arch's form 28 Nov 01:30Z; Fable r7c: the massif floats, an empty sand band between its foot and the corals): the key frame's massif was two kit heads stacked in depth (layout.json b0 at 4.7 m in front of b3 at 12.5 m), so its foot overlapped the corals. Same relation here with the kit's own heads in the mid-ground, overlapping the arch's foot in frame, the gate left clear: at ~25 % of the frame width, 10 m; r9b (Fable r9: equal mushrooms bracketing the gate read as kit stamping, and the near layer still unlinked): nearer at 7.6 m, x1.3, stem sunk 0.4 m, turned 70 deg, so its base overlaps the coral group's tops
